title: Service credit simulation API and stewardship spec
author: Priya Raman
content:
Overview

This design spec defines the Service Credit Simulation API and the associated stewardship workflows used by Redwood product, billing, and engineering teams to model, validate, and sanction crediting decisions for consumption-based products (hosted API tokens, embeddings, fidelity credits, preemptible capacity). The Simulator is intended to be the canonical offline model for estimating customer-facing credit behavior before changes land in pricing, credit-escrow, or SLA systems.

Goals

- Provide an authoritative, reproducible simulation of crediting outcomes for a given set of customer accounts, routes, and traffic traces.
- Surface economic regressions (cost-to-serve, effective revenue) for proposed crediting rule changes before deployment.
- Support per-route and per-tenant fidelity mappings and multi-variant fallback paths.
- Produce machine-readable reports and a lightweight API for integration with the Console, Sales quoting tools, and the CI pipeline.

Non-goals

- This system is not the runtime enforcement mechanism for crediting (that remains the Billing/Runtime crediting engine).
- Not intended to replace full financial audits; it is a decision support tool.

Scope and Stakeholders

- Primary consumers: Product (owner), Pricing, Sales Engineering, Finance, and Billing infra teams.
- Integrations: Redwood Console (usage preview UI), Billing Sandbox, CI experiment runners, and feature-flag rollout service.
- Data inputs: historical usage traces (token & embedding tokens/time-series), model latency/cost profiles, capacity tier pricing, and fidelity mapping tables.

Key Concepts

- Credit Unit: the smallest billable unit (e.g., generation token, embedding vector, fidelity-credit).
- Crediting Rule: a deterministic mapping that converts a request trace into credited units (including refunds, tier discounts, pro-rata adjustments).
- Stewardship Policy: human-approvable guardrails for rule changes.

API Contract (summary)

The Simulation API exposes three endpoints: /simulate, /validate, /report. Example request/response skeletons are shown below (pseudo-JSON). The Simulator is read-only relative to live billing.

POST /api/v1/simulate
Request body (pseudo):
{
  "account_id": "acct_12345",
  "time_range": "2026-06-01/2026-06-30",
  "trace_source": "historical|synthetic",
  "crediting_ruleset_id": "rule_v2_candidate",
  "variant_fallbacks": ["modelA-small","modelA-quant"],
  "options": {"include_overhead": true, "simulate_skew": "regional"}
}

Response (pseudo):
{
  "simulation_id": "sim_abc123",
  "summary": {"total_credits": 123456, "estimated_cost": 3214.50, "effective_price_per_1k": 25.97},
  "per_route_breakdown": [{"route": "/v1/generate", "credits": 100000, "cost": 2100.00}, ...]
}

POST /api/v1/validate
Request body (pseudo):
{
  "simulation_id": "sim_abc123",
  "assertions": ["total_cost < 3500", "p95_latency_increase < 10%"],
  "requested_by": "pricing@redwood.ai"
}

Response (pseudo):
{
  "validation_id": "val_321",
  "status": "passed|failed",
  "failures": ["p95_latency_increase: 12% (threshold 10%)"]
}

GET /api/v1/report/{simulation_id}
- Returns a signed CSV/JSON report suitable for finance ingestion and a human-readable summary for Console display.

Data model and important fields (table)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| simulation_id | string | Unique id for run |
| trace_id | string | Identifier for input trace or synthetic profile |
| credited_units | integer | Number of credit units produced by ruleset |
| estimated_cost_usd | decimal | Cost to Redwood to serve these units (model+infra) |
| effective_customer_price_usd | decimal | Hypothetical charged amount given pricing slab |
| delta_revenue | decimal | Estimated revenue delta (price - cost) |
| rule_version | string | Crediting ruleset version used |

Functional requirements (must)

1) Determinism: Given the same inputs, the simulator returns bitwise-identical credit accounting results.
2) Replayability: Support both historical trace replay and synthetic traffic generation with configurable randomness seeds.
3) Multi-variant support: Model fallback and variant substitution must be simulated with realistic latency and fallback costs.
4) Time-windowed aggregation: Produce hourly and daily aggregations, including p50/p95/p99 latencies and cost distributions.
5) Performance: A 30-day account trace with 10M requests must complete simulation in under 20 minutes on standard infra used by CI runners.
6) Auditability: Every simulation must include provenance metadata: who ran it, which ruleset, input trace hash, and steward approval state if applicable.

Non-functional requirements

- Security: Inputs may contain customer identifiers; service must be ACL-protected and support data redaction in Console exports.
- Retention: Simulation artifacts kept for 90 days by default; extended retention to 2 years by request.
- Observability: Expose internal metrics (sim_run_time_seconds, sim_error_rate, sim_memory_bytes) and structured logs with trace_id.
- Cost: Simulator infra should be cost-capped; background batch runs scheduled during off-peak and throttled.

Stewardship Workflow (human-in-the-loop)

1. Author creates a candidate Crediting Ruleset (CRS) in the Ruleset Registry.
2. Run /simulate for representative tenant and global samples.
3. Run /validate assertions. If validation passes, request Stewardship review.
4. Stewardship panel receives auto-generated report and mitigations.
5. Stewardship approves, rejects, or requests rollback changes. Approved rulesets are promoted to staging for Canary trials.

Rollout and Canary Plan

- Phase 0 (Sandbox): internal runs for feature parity; no billing implications (now).
- Phase 1 (Staging): promote approved rulesets to a small set of low-impact tenants (5–10 customers) with observability hooks.
- Phase 2 (Canary): 0.5–2% of traffic self-serve customers; monitor revenue, unit cost, error budget.
- Phase 3 (Gradual ramp): 10%, 30%, 70%, 100% with 24–72 hour holds at each step and automatic rollback triggers (p95 latency +10% or revenue delta -20%).

Metrics and SLOs

- Simulation latency SLO: 95% of simulations complete in < 20 minutes for 30-day, 10M request traces.
- Accuracy SLO: Estimated cost vs observed cost during a 30-day mirror test should drift < 8%.
- Availability: API 99.9% for internal users.

Monitoring and Alerts

- Alerts: sim_error_rate > 0.5% over 30m, sim_run_time_seconds p95 > 25m, validation_failures spike > 3x baseline.
- Dashboard: per-team usage, average delta_revenue, and a list of recent steward decisions.

Security and Compliance

- Access: RBAC restricted to product, pricing, finance, and approved engineering SREs.
- Data handling: Support PII redaction toggle; do not store raw request payloads longer than retention window.
- Audit logs: Persist steward approvals and simulation inputs with nonce.

Backward compatibility and migration notes

- Ruleset schema is versioned (v1, v2…). Simulator must accept older schema and map to v2 for parity checks.
- All promoted rulesets produce a compatibility report prior to deployment.

Open questions

- How granular should tenant sampling be for global predictions (per-tenant vs cohort)? Proposed interim: cohort by 8 revenue deciles.
- Should the simulator incorporate predicted model degradation due to quantization over time, or treat quantization as a static delta? Proposed: static delta for initial launch.

Checklist before merging to main

- [ ] Implementation: API endpoints, runner, and report generator complete.
- [ ] E2E tests: determinism, replayability, and synthetic seed coverage.
- [ ] Observability: dashboards and alerts wired.
- [ ] Stewardship UI: Console card for submit/approve flows.
- [ ] Security review: RBAC and data redaction validated.
- [ ] Finance sign-off: sample reports validated for ingestion.

Appendix: Implementation snippets

- Synthetic trace generator CLI (example):
redwood-sim generate --seed 42 --profile transactional-high --duration 30d > sample-trace.json

- Minimal simulation run (curl):
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
  https://internal-api.redwood.ai/api/v1/simulate -d '{"account_id":"acct_12345","time_range":"2026-06-01/2026-06-30","trace_source":"synthetic","crediting_ruleset_id":"rule_v2_candidate"}'
